sequence_notes.rule: Veo's camera is locked; Premiere adds the handheld sway and any push, eased.
sequence_notes.why: Omni camera moves drift and redraw

sequence_notes.rule: Masked crew: no lip-sync. Only the minister (bare face) is synced, with lip-sync-dub.
One actor moves per shot; the rest of the motion is the van's sway, the rain and the lights.
sequence_notes.why: Omni struggles past about three movers

sequence_notes.rule: The monitor's numbers and the flat line are never asked of Veo as readable text; if the screen comes out as slop it is covered with a drawn trace in Premiere.
Timing to the voices (~14 s): A 0-5.5 (three lines overlap), B 5.5-7 ("Why have we stopped?!"), C 7-10.5 (the minister), D 10.5-14 ("Fifty over twen-", flatline, black, logo).
sequence_notes.why: voices are cut, one file per line, in audio/voices

frames.job: Throw the viewer into the fight for his life: urgency at full speed before anything stops it.

options.label: She shouts forward
options.idea: The paramedic twists from the monitor towards the cab and shouts, gripping the yellow rail as the van sways; the trace races; behind her the second paramedic works on the patient. Premiere: handheld sway, a 4% push.

lanes.does: her turn and shout, the sway, the trace

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. Inside a speeding ambulance at night. The paramedic in the surgical mask twists from the heart monitor towards the cab and shouts forward, her gloved hand gripping the yellow grab rail as the whole compartment sways from side to side. The green trace on the monitor races. Behind her the second paramedic keeps pressing on the patient's chest. Blue light flickers through the windscreen. Filmed like real handheld news footage, quick movements blurring the way a film camera blurs them. One continuous shot, no cuts, no dialogue, no text. The camera does not move. Thanks.
options.cut: in on the cut from black at 0:00, out at 5.5 s on the brakes
options.risk: the monitor's numbers may smear into slop; the man behind may stop moving

options.label: Eyes on the monitor
options.idea: She leans in to the monitor, close, not shouting yet; the van rocks; the voices play over her. Quieter dread, the shouting carried by sound. Premiere: a hard push on her eyes.

lanes.does: her lean in, the sway, the trace

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. Inside a speeding ambulance at night. The masked paramedic leans in close to the heart monitor, eyes fixed on the racing green trace, braced against the sway of the compartment with one gloved hand on the yellow rail. The overhead strip lights shiver as the van rocks over the road. Filmed like real handheld news footage, quick movements blurring the way a film camera blurs them. One continuous shot, no cuts, no dialogue, no text. The camera does not move. Thanks.

frames.job: The stop: the whole short's injustice in one image, a raised glove holding back a dying man.

options.label: The glove holds
options.idea: The wipers sweep once, the outrider holds his glove up and does not move, the blue lights pulse on the wet glass; the driver's hands tighten on the wheel.

lanes.does: one wiper sweep, beacon pulse, the driver's hands

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. Looking through the rain-streaked windscreen of a stopped ambulance at night. The police outrider on his motorcycle holds one gloved hand raised, perfectly still. The wiper sweeps once across the glass. Blue emergency light pulses over the wet windscreen and rain runs down it. On the steering wheel, the driver's hands slowly tighten their grip. Filmed like real handheld news footage, quick movements blurring the way a film camera blurs them. One continuous shot, no cuts, no dialogue, no text. The camera does not move. Thanks.
options.cut: 5.5 s to 7 s; the rest of the clip is spare
options.risk: the wiper may redraw the outrider; keep the cut short

options.label: Headlights cross
options.idea: The same hold, and behind the outrider a big black car's headlights slide across from the left: the minister arriving, seen before we cut to him.

frames.job: The beneficiary: the man the ambulance waits for, comfortable, on the phone about canapés.

options.label: Keep pl-04, re-sync to Charon
options.idea: The round 1 clip pl-04-MIN1-b, muted, lip-synced to the new Charon line with lip-sync-dub; the glass muffle is on the audio.
options.risk: Charon's line (2.4 s) is a different rhythm from Orus; if the mouth can't match, cut to the jar of lemon curd as the cutaway

frames.job: The cost, and the button: he dies, and the world doesn't stop.

options.label: The light turns green
options.idea: Nobody moves. The paramedic's hands stay on the still chest. Through the windscreen, the red traffic light turns green and the cars ahead pull away. The world moves on the moment he's gone.

lanes.does: the light changes, distant cars move off
lock-off, then black and the logo
a drawn flat trace if the screen is slop

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. Inside a stopped ambulance at night, looking down the compartment to the windscreen. The paramedic stays completely still with his hands resting on the old man's chest. Far ahead through the windscreen, the red traffic light changes to green, and the blurred tail lights of the cars ahead begin to pull away into the rain. The monitor glows with a flat line. Filmed like real handheld news footage, quick movements blurring the way a film camera blurs them. One continuous shot, no cuts, no dialogue, no text. The camera does not move. Thanks.
options.cut: 10.5 s to 13 s, then black and the logo
options.risk: the light change may not land in time; the small far-off light may smear

options.label: He sits back
options.idea: He stops pressing and slowly sits back on his heels, looking at the monitor; the strip light buzzes. Plain and human.

lanes.does: a drawn flat trace if needed

options.veo_prompt: The camera does not move. Inside a stopped ambulance at night. The masked paramedic slowly takes his hands off the old man's chest and sits back, looking up at the monitor, which shows a flat line. The overhead strip light flickers once. Red light from the traffic signal lies across the ceiling. Filmed like real handheld news footage, quick movements blurring the way a film camera blurs them. One continuous shot, no cuts, no dialogue, no text. The camera does not move. Thanks.
